From Scarlatti to Schubert: The Evolution of the Piano Sonata. Acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a remarkable recital.

The Italian Embassy is delighted to present internationally acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a recital exploring the remarkable evolution of the piano sonata through the music of Domenico Scarlatti, Ludwig van Beethoven, and Franz Schubert.

Spanning more than a century of musical innovation, the programme traces the transformation of the sonata from Scarlatti's elegant miniatures to Beethoven's groundbreaking masterpieces and Schubert's poetic lyricism. Featuring Beethoven's celebrated "Waldstein" Sonata and his final Piano Sonata in C minor, Op. 111, this recital offers a compelling journey through some of the greatest works ever written for the piano.

Renowned for his interpretations of the Classical and Romantic repertoire, Christian Leotta rose to international prominence at the age of 22 after performing the complete cycle of Beethoven's 32 Piano Sonatas. Since then, he has appeared in more than 50 countries and performed with leading orchestras in many of the world's most prestigious concert halls.

long_description:
Overview

Share ceremonial cacao, heartfelt conversation and a nourishing dinner in an evening of authentic connection and presence.

Cacao & Connection Circle
Starts at 6pm

This evening is an invitation to slow down, be present, and experience genuine human connection. Together we'll share ceremonial cacao, meaningful conversation, and a welcoming space where there's no need to perform, impress, or have all the right words. Just come as you are.

What to Expect

We'll begin with a gentle grounding practice to help everyone arrive. This is an opportunity to pause, settle into the present moment, and reconnect with yourself before connecting with others.

From there, we'll gather in a circle to share ceremonial cacao. 

We'll then move into a heart-sharing circle. A thoughtful question will be offered as a prompt, and you're warmly invited, but never expected to share your experience. There is no advice-giving or fixing here. Instead, we practise honest expression, deep listening, and creating space for one another to simply be witnessed.

What Heart-Sharing Can Offer

 Authentic Connection

Experience the kind of connection that comes from being seen, heard, and accepted exactly as you are.

Meaningful Conversation

Step beyond everyday small talk into conversations that invite honesty, curiosity, and presence.

Greater Self-Awareness

Sharing and listening often brings unexpected clarity about your own thoughts, emotions, and life experiences.

Gentle Personal Growth

Speaking from the heart and listening without judgement can quietly shift perspectives and deepen understanding.

A Sense of Belonging

Being part of a supportive circle can ease feelings of isolation and remind us that we all share common human experiences.

 

After the circle, we'll enjoy a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert together, both included in your ticket. It's a relaxed time to continue conversations, connect naturally, and simply enjoy each other's company.

Meet Andre, your host:

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Create a team that communicates better, takes ownership, and solves problems together.

A conversation goes sideways. Someone starts blaming. Another person steps in to fix everything. Before long, the real issue has been lost and the same pattern begins again.

This free leadership session will help you recognise those patterns and respond differently.

Leadership: Escape the Drama Triangle is a practical 90-minute workshop for business owners and team leaders who want their people to communicate clearly, take greater ownership, and solve problems together.

You will learn how to:

Recognise the Drama Triangle in everyday team conversations
Identify when people are operating below the line
Avoid rescuing, blaming or taking over
Reframe conversations so people can take responsibility
Create clearer, more productive team discussions
Help your team move from problems towards practical next steps

This is not about removing every disagreement from your workplace.

It is about giving you a simple way to recognise unhelpful patterns early and guide the conversation towards a better outcome.

You will leave with practical language and ideas you can begin using with your team straight away.

Anyone who finds themselves stepping in to solve everyone else’s problems

Overview

Refresh body and mind with a gentle spring breathwork journey to release winter heaviness and reconnect with your natural aliveness.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Renewal




Event starts at 6pm

September is a threshold month, a natural invitation to spring clean.

Not just the space around you, but the space inside you too.

Spring Cleansing is a somatic breathwork session designed to help you gently shift some of the heaviness that can build up over the colder months. Think sluggishness, brain fog, tension, low energy, or simply that feeling of being a little stuck in your body.

Through a consent-led, trauma-aware breathwork journey, we’ll create space to:

move stagnant energy and emotions
warm and reconnect with the body
release some of the heaviness that winter can leave behind
return to your breath, presence, and natural sense of aliveness

A chance to pause, breathe, and make room for something new.

You’ll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and more connected to your body, like opening the windows and letting fresh air move through.

This session is for you if:
you’ve felt heavy, puffy, sluggish, or “damp” after winter
your chest/breath has felt tight, shallow, or restricted
you’ve been waking up tired, unmotivated, or mentally foggy
you’ve been indoors more, moving less, and can feel it in your body
you want a reset that’s embodied, not performative
you want a welcoming, choice-based space to explore breathwork
What to expect
Arrival (consent + information) chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Nervous system primer: clearing and activation safely
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc. clearing, warming, and releasing what’s been holding on
Optional movement to support circulation (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)
Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and clearer head
more warmth and circulation through chest/shoulders/hips
improved mood and motivation
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a renewed sense of momentum that feels steady (not forced)
Please bring:
Yoga mat
Warm layers (we’ll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen
If you run cold, bring a blanket
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there’s anything you’d like to share before the session.
Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy; serious cardiovascular conditions; uncontrolled blood pressure; glaucoma or retinal detachment; epilepsy or seizure history; recent surgery or concussion; or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours, reach out if you need support.

You’ll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24–48 hours after the session (gentle regulation, grounding, and integration).

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!

This is for you if you want nervous-system-led guidance to:

soften chronic tension patterns in the body
build embodied boundaries and self-trust
move through stuckness with breath, somatic tools, and grounded coaching

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Her work combines somatic breathwork, Reiki, and life coaching to support nervous system regulation, emotional wellbeing, and grounded personal transformation in a practical, trauma-aware way.

This workshop offers helpful information for Family/Whānau about death and dying. Advance care planning and community resources will be discussed.




Many people find it difficult to talk about dying, yet dying is an important stage of life and is inevitable. We plan for the birth of a child, yet when it comes to the end of life, we don’t often want to think about it or talk about it.




Having a plan outlines our care preferences for the future. Having an Advance Care Plan (ACP) that aligns with our beliefs and values, is a gift that we can give to our family / whānau.




We will explore:


Why is it hard to talk about death and dying?

What to expect when someone is dying

Supports available

Overview

A provocation from inside and outside: addressing New Zealand’s systems challenges

Join us for the next lecture in our current seminar series

Over recent decades, New Zealand policy making in most areas has been focused on the short-term: often political claims for solutions have been over-simplified. This has contributed to citizen’s cynicism and a decline in institutional trust which puts at risk the social cohesion which has been one of New Zealand’s greatest assets. Most evident is the continued failure to really lift productivity and reach a trajectory like other small, advanced economies.

The challenges ahead of us include: a big demographic shift in age and composition and the need for a more complete population strategy, the failure to systematically understand the opportunities in the rapid technology revolution underway in both the digital/AI and life sciences, an inevitable shift in the nature of higher education, a persistent failure of Auckland to demonstrate a comparative agglomeration effect, a failure to maximise international partnerships beyond trade and security, and a continued naive exceptionalism with regard to science and research. At the policy level this is reflected in a relative lack of the use of the tools of long-term thinking including anticipatory foresight and formative evaluation and continued siloed and short-term biases in the budget process.

Our guest speaker - Sir Peter Gluckman, founder of Koi Tū: Centre for Informed Futures and the President of International Science Council - will address each of these provocations.

About this event

This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.

If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.

About the presenter

Sir Peter Gluckman ONZ KNZM FRSNZ FRS is founder of Koi Tu: Centre for Informed Futures (a non-partisan thinktank focused on long-term and complex issues facing New Zealand), president of the International Science Council and member of the Prime Minister’s Science, Innovation and Technology Advisory Council. Former President of the International Network for Government Science Advice and chief science advisor to the Prime Ministers of New Zealand (2009-2018). He chaired both the recent Science System Advisory Group and the University Advisory Group.

He is a biomedical and clinical scientist who has published over 750 scientific papers and was awarded the Rutherford Medal in 2001 and has written extensively on the science policy and science diplomacy interfaces. He is the recipient of the American Association for the Advancement of Science medal for science diplomacy.

About this seminar series

New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.

This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.

Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.

Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.

For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz
